sources.content: Proposal GRW-55: passive health checks for Garrowind. Garrowind, our layer 4 load balancer, checks backends only with active TCP probes every 10 seconds. A backend that accepts connections but resets them under load stays in rotation, and in May one such host failed 30 percent of requests for 2 hours. This proposal adds passive checks: Garrowind will eject a backend after 5 consecutive connection failures seen in real traffic. The networking team owns the work and tracks it in its third quarter plan.

An ejected backend stays out of rotation for 30 seconds, and the time doubles each time it is ejected again, up to 5 minutes. Garrowind never ejects more than 50 percent of the backends in a pool at once, so a broad failure cannot empty the pool. Active TCP probes continue unchanged. Operators turn the feature on per pool with passive_checks: enabled. The first release ships it off by default, and the team will review ejection logs from two pools before changing the default.

claims.text: Garrowind may eject up to 75 percent of a pool's backends at once.
Garrowind's active TCP probes run every 10 seconds.
An ejected Garrowind backend first stays out of rotation for 30 seconds.
Garrowind's first release ships passive checks off by default.
Under the proposal, Garrowind ejects a backend after 3 consecutive connection failures.
Garrowind is a layer 4 load balancer.
